interest: Tracks Japan's prewar tobacco monopoly pricing and the shift from pipe tobacco to Western cigarettes.
overview: This file consists of an extensive voluntary consular report (Report No. 180) prepared by American Consul A. F. Tower and approved by Consul General Arthur Garrels at the American Consulate General in Tokyo in February 1937, entitled 'Japanese Tobacco Monopoly Revenues Increased.' The report analyzes price increases decreed on November 11, 1936, by the Imperial Japanese Monopoly Bureau across manufactured tobacco products and examines their expected contribution to state revenue. It provides comprehensive statistical tables detailing wholesale and retail price changes, dealer discount adjustments, domestic leaf tobacco production and grading trends (highlighting the shift from native varieties to Virginia-type leaf), foreign leaf imports, and the import, export, and domestic distribution of manufactured tobacco products from 1932 through late 1936.

subfiles.about: A voluntary consular report detailing price hikes, domestic production trends, and foreign trade statistics of the Japanese tobacco monopoly in early 1937.
subfiles.summary: Consul A. F. Tower reports on the significant price increases imposed on November 11, 1936, by the Imperial Japanese Monopoly Bureau across almost all domestic and imported manufactured tobacco products, calculated to generate an additional 25 to 31 million yen in state profits annually while lowering retail dealer commission discounts. Detailed price schedules are presented for individual cigarette and cut-tobacco brands, along with imported American and British smoking products. The report analyzes leaf tobacco cultivation in Japan Proper, identifying a growing preference for mouthpiece-free Virginia cigarettes over native Japanese leaf types, and provides thorough statistical tabulations covering leaf procurement, foreign leaf imports, leaf exports, and manufactured tobacco imports, exports, and domestic sales from 1932 through late 1936.
subfiles.title: Japanese Tobacco Monopoly Revenues Increased (Consular Report No. 180)
